### Temperature at 200-300m Depth

```{r}

source("_common.R")
```

```{r}
#| include: false

# Set path to variable: Temperature_at_Depth
# This is where the data are and where the plots will go
Dir <- here("Temperature_at_Depth")
# Check if it exists; if not, create it
if (!dir.exists(Dir)) {
  dir.create(Dir)
}
```

```{r}
#| include: false
### Load data
# Monthly temperature
TatD_full <- read.csv(file = paste0(Dir, '/T_at_200300_ts.dat'), skip = 9, header = FALSE) %>% 
  rename(Date_Time=V1, TatD_degC=V2) %>% 
  mutate(Date_Time=dmy_hm(Date_Time))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# Remove seasonal means to calculate anomalies
TatD_climo <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(TatD_full), ncol = 1)
for (m in seq(1,12,1)) {
  mo_of_int <- which(month(TatD_full$Date_Time) == m)
  TatD_climo[mo_of_int,1] <- mean(TatD_full$TatD_degC[mo_of_int])
}

TatD_anom_ts <- TatD_full$TatD_degC - TatD_climo
```

```{r}
#| include: false
### Linear fit 
# Note that this assumes that observations are equally spaced in time, which they're  not
n_obs <- seq(1, length(TatD_full$TatD_degC), 1)
TatD_lm <- lm(TatD_full$TatD_degC ~ n_obs)
TatD_anom_lm <- lm(TatD_anom_ts ~ n_obs)

# Change over time
delta_TatD_lm <- TatD_lm$fitted.values[length(n_obs)] - TatD_lm$fitted.values[1]

delta_TatD_anom_lm <- TatD_anom_lm$fitted.values[length(n_obs)] - TatD_anom_lm$fitted.values[1]
```

```{r}
#| include: false
### Annual values
TatD_full <- TatD_full %>% 
    mutate(Year=year(Date_Time), 
           Anom=TatD_anom_ts)

ann_TatD <- TatD_full %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(TatD_degC = mean(TatD_degC, na.rm = TRUE))
ann_anom <- TatD_full %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(Anom = mean(Anom, na.rm = TRUE))
ann_mean_RptYr <- ann_TatD$TatD_degC[which(ann_TatD$Year == RptYr)]
ann_anom_RptYr <- ann_anom$Anom[which(ann_TatD$Year == RptYr)]
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
# Note that the above needs to be 'echo' and not 'include' so that the error checks print.

# This section includes some error checks to prompt fixing the text
if (any(summary(TatD_lm)$coefficients[,4] > 0.05)) {
  print('The linear fit to monthly values is not signficant. Remove text related to the linear trend.')
}

if (any(summary(TatD_anom_lm)$coefficients[,4] > 0.05)) {
  print('The linear fit to anomaly values is not signficant. Remove text related to the linear trend.')
}

# Pull out the MONTHLY values we need for the report & plots
yr_of_int <- which(TatD_full$Year == RptYr)
prev_yrs <- which(TatD_full$Year < RptYr)
all_yrs <- which(TatD_full$Year <= RptYr)
monthly_max_RptYr <- max(TatD_full$TatD_degC[yr_of_int])
monthly_min_RptYr <- min(TatD_full$TatD_degC[yr_of_int])
monthly_max_PrevYrs <- max(TatD_full$TatD_degC[prev_yrs])
monthly_min_PrevYrs <- min(TatD_full$TatD_degC[prev_yrs])

if (monthly_max_RptYr > monthly_max_PrevYrs) {
  print('The greatest monthly value was during the report year.  Revise text to reflect this.')
}

if (monthly_min_RptYr < monthly_min_PrevYrs) {
  print('The lowest monthly value was during the report year.  Revise text to reflect this.')
}
```

```{r}
ann_TatD$`Degrees C` <- format(round(ann_TatD$`Degrees C`, digits=2), nsmall = 2)
```

```{r}
TatD_dashboard <- TatD_full %>% 
  mutate(Month=month(Date_Time), 
         ID='TatD', 
         Value_lm=TatD_lm$fitted.values, 
         Anom_lm=NA, # No anomaly for this variable  #TatD_anom_lm$fitted.values, 
         Units='Deg C',
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# Borrowing code from the dashboard for this chunk
# so that figures look the same across products
indicator_data <- TatD_dashboard |>
  filter(Year <= RptYr)

# Create color palette for easy reference 
pal <- c(oceans[3], coral[2], waves[2], coral[3], crustacean[2])

# Calculate annual means 
ann_vals <- indicator_data |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(Value = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE))

# Identify the current year, to overlay on plot
given_yr <- indicator_data |>
  filter(Year == RptYr)

given_yr_ann <- bind_cols(Value = rep(ann_vals$Value[dim(ann_vals)[1]]),
                          Date_Time = given_yr$Date_Time,
                          Anom = ann_anom$`Anom`[which(ann_anom$Year == RptYr)])

# x axis ticks and grid
# Made a sequence instead so we don't have to manually update it every five years
x_grid <- c(seq.POSIXt(min(indicator_data$Date_Time), max(indicator_data$Date_Time), by='5 year'))

# y-axis limits
ts_y_lim <-c(10.8, 11.7)

# Plot using ggplot
legendInfo <- as.factor(c(paste0('Mothly average, 1980-', RptYr-2), 
                          paste0('Annual average, 1980-', RptYr-2), 
                          paste0('Mothly average, ', RptYr-1), 
                          paste0('Annual average, ', RptYr-1),
                          paste0('Long-term Trend')))
levels(legendInfo) <- levels(legendInfo)[c(4,5,1,2,3)] # To arrange in preferred order for the legend, otherwise it's alphabetical

p <- ggplot() +
  geom_path(data=indicator_data, aes(Date_Time, Value, color=legendInfo[2])) +
  geom_path(data=ann_vals, aes(dmy_hm(paste0('01-01-',Year,' 00:00')), Value, color=legendInfo[5])) +
  geom_path(data=indicator_data, aes(Date_Time, Value_lm, color=legendInfo[3])) +
  geom_path(data=given_yr, aes(Date_Time, Value, color=legendInfo[4])) +
  geom_path(data=given_yr_ann, aes(Date_Time, Value, color=legendInfo[1])) +
  scale_x_datetime(breaks = x_grid, date_labels = '%Y', expand = F) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = F, limits = ts_y_lim, breaks=(seq(min(ts_y_lim),max(ts_y_lim),by=0.1))) +
  scale_color_manual(name=NULL, values=pal[c(1,3,5,2,4)]) +
  ylab('200-300 m Temperature (°C)') +
  xlab('Year') +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
  plotTheme

#ggsave(paste0(Dir, '/TempAtDepth_ts_', RptYr, '_ggolot.pdf'), plot=p, width=6, height=5, units='in')
#ggsave(paste0(Dir, '/TempAtDepth_ts_', RptYr, '_ggolot.png'), plot=p, width=6, height=5, units='in')
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| include: false


library(rnaturalearth)
library(terra)
library(tidyterra)
library(sf)
library(metR)


# Or use spatial data to plot so you can change the projection 
# For this you have to use the original ncdf files that are used in map_data_for_dashboard.R file
currYr <- rast(file.path(Dir, paste0('T_at_200300_yr', RptYr, '.nc')))
climo <- rast(file.path(Dir, 'T_at_200300_climo_1980thru2009.nc'))
anom <- currYr - climo
# Make it an eckert IV projection centered on 180 long
eckert_iv <- "+proj=eck4 +lon_0=180 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"
# Transform the chl anomaly to eckert IV
anom_eckert <- project(anom, eckert_iv)
curr_eckert <- project(currYr, eckert_iv)

# Make the longline box. This will automatically project as eckert on the plot
box_sf <- st_polygon(list(matrix(c(180, 15,  # Bottom-left
                                   240, 15,  # Bottom-right
                                   240, 45,  # Top-right
                                   180, 45,  # Top-left
                                   180, 15   # Close back at start
                                   ), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE))) %>%
  st_sfc(crs = 4326)
# Segmentize it so it can curve
LLbox <- box_sf %>%
  st_set_crs(NA) %>%
  st_segmentize(dfMaxLength = 0.5) %>%
  st_set_crs(4326) %>%
  st_sf()

# Get land
world_land <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>% 
  st_break_antimeridian(lon_0 = 180) %>%  # This splits land geometries at the map's 180-degree boundary split
  st_make_valid()
# Create a curved map outline polygon (WGS84) for the tapering map border
map_outline_sf <- st_polygon(list(matrix(c(
    119.75, -0.25,  
    260.25, -0.25,  
    260.25, 55.25,  
    119.75, 55.25,  
    119.75, -0.25   
  ), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE))) %>% 
  st_sfc(crs = 4326) %>% 
  st_set_crs(NA) %>% 
  st_segmentize(dfMaxLength = 0.5) %>% 
  st_set_crs(4326) %>% 
  st_sf()
# Transform both land and map border to Eckert IV and slice the land cleanly
map_outline_projected <- st_transform(map_outline_sf, eckert_iv)
world_land_projected  <- st_transform(world_land, eckert_iv)
# This physically cuts the land boundaries to match the curved outline frame
world_land_clipped <- st_intersection(world_land_projected, map_outline_projected)
# Create custom dataframes for the labels, shifted slightly outward in degrees
# Left side labels (at Lon 119.75, shifted slightly West to ~116.5)
labels_left <- st_as_sf(data.frame(
    lon = 116.5, 
    lat = c(0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50), 
    text = c("0°", "10°N", "20°N", "30°N", "40°N", "50°N")
), coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
# Bottom labels (at Lat -0.25, shifted slightly South to ~ -2.5)
labels_bottom <- st_as_sf(data.frame(
    lon = c(120, 150, 180, 210, 240), 
    lat = -2.5, 
    text = c("120°E","150°E", "180°", "150°W", "120°W")
), coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
# Convert raster to data frame for contour labeling
curr_df <- as_tibble(curr_eckert, xy = TRUE)

# Make the plot
p_map <- ggplot() +
  # Raster Background
  geom_spatraster(data = anom_eckert) +
  geom_spatraster_contour(data= curr_eckert, color = "gray30", breaks = seq(0,20,by=5), show.legend=F, linewidth=0.5, linetype='dashed') +
  geom_text_contour(
        data = curr_df,
        aes(x = x, y = y, z = TATD_2025),
        breaks = seq(0, 20, by = 5),
        color = "gray30",
        size = 5,
        min.size = 75,   # Increase this threshold to drop short island contours
        skip = 0,         # Draw labels on all remaining long lines
        label.placer = label_placer_fraction(frac = 0.5) # Place label in the middle of long lines
    ) +
  # Colorbar configured for top placement with labels on top
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = oceans[2], mid = "white", high = coral[2], 
                       midpoint = 0, 
                       limits=c(-4,4), 
                       oob=scales::squish,
        name = "SST Anomaly (°C)",
        na.value = 'transparent',
        guide = guide_colorbar(
          direction = "horizontal",    # Forces horizontal bar layout
          barwidth = unit(0.7, "npc"), # Spans width of map
          barheight = unit(10, "pt"),  # Controls the thickness of the bar
          title.position = "top",      # Positions "CHL" above the scale
          title.hjust = 0.5,           # Centers the title text
          label.position = "top",      # Forces the numeric values (0.0, 0.1, etc.) ABOVE the bar
          label.hjust = 0.5),
        ) +
  # Clipped Land & Boxes
  geom_sf(data = world_land_clipped, fill = "gray80", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = map_outline_projected, fill = NA, color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = LLbox, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.75) + # longline area box
  
  # Add longline text box
  geom_sf_text(
    data = st_as_sf(data.frame(lon = 180, lat = 45), coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326),
    aes(label = "Longline fishing grounds"),
    size = 6,
    vjust = -0.5,       # Pushes the text slightly ABOVE the top line of the box
    hjust = 0,          # Left-aligns the text starting from the 180° corner
    fontface = "bold",  # Makes it look clean and distinct from coordinate labels
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # Manual curved labels to follow the map shape
  geom_sf_text(data = labels_left, aes(label = text), size = 5, hjust = 1, color = "gray30") +
  geom_sf_text(data = labels_bottom, aes(label = text), size = 5, vjust = 1, color = "gray30") +
  
  coord_sf(
    crs = eckert_iv,
    xlim = c(ext(curr_eckert)[1], ext(curr_eckert)[2]),
    ylim = c(ext(curr_eckert)[3], ext(curr_eckert)[4]), 
    expand = FALSE, 
    clip = "off" # clip = "off" tells ggplot to render text that sits outside the map boundary box
    ) + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_blank(),
    # Remove square plot border
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    panel.grid=element_blank(), 
    # Remove grid lines
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(), # Turn off the default rectangular system text labels completely
    # Relocate legend above the figure
    legend.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"), # Font size/style for "Chl Anomaly..."
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),                 # Font size for "-0.6", "0", "0.6", etc.
    legend.position = "top",          # Relocates the whole legend unit below the map
    legend.justification = c(0.42,0.5),     # Centers it perfectly underneath
    legend.box.margin = margin(b = 0.5),  # Adds clean padding between the bottom map labels and the color bar
    # Buffer the margins a little for the custom labels
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 30, 40)) +
  xlab(NULL) + 
  ylab(NULL)
```

**Rationale:** The temperature at 200–300 m reflects the temperature in the mid-range of depths targeted by the deep-set bigeye tuna fishery. Bigeye have preferred thermal habitat, generally staying within temperatures ranging from 8–14 °C while they are at depth [@Howell2010-rq]. Changes in ocean temperature at depth will impact tuna, and in turn, potentially impact their catchability. Understanding the drivers of sub-surface temperature trends and their ecosystem impacts is an area of active research.  

**Status:** In `r RptYr`, 200–300 m temperatures ranged from `r signif(monthly_min_RptYr, 4)`–`r signif(monthly_max_RptYr, 4)` °C with an average value of `r signif(ann_mean_RptYr,4)` °C. These temperatures are within the range of temperatures experienced over the past several decades (`r signif(monthly_min_PrevYrs, 4)`–`r signif(monthly_max_PrevYrs, 4)` °C) and are within the bounds of bigeye tuna’s preferred deep daytime thermal habitat (8–14 °C). Over the period of record (1980–`r RptYr`), 200–300 m temperatures have declined by `r abs(signif(delta_TatD_lm, 1))` °C. The spatial pattern of temperature anomalies was mixed with temperatures at depth just north of the main Hawaiian Islands roughly 0.5–1.5 °C below average, and temperatures north and west of the Hawaiian Islands 0.5-2 °C above average.   

**Description:** Ocean temperature at 200–300 m depth is averaged across the Hawaiʻi-based longline fishing grounds (15° – 45°N, 180° – 120°W). Global Ocean Data Assimilation System (GODAS) data are used. GODAS incorporates global ocean data from moorings, expendable bathythermographs (XBTs), and Argo floats.   

**Timeframe:** Annual, monthly.  

**Region/Location:** Hawaii longline region: 15° – 45°N, 180° – 120°W.  

**Measurement Platform:** _In-situ_ sensors, model.  

**Sourced from:** @NOAA2026-vs and @APDRC2026-ft. Graphics produced in part using @Stawitz2026-kw. NCEP Global Ocean Data Assimilation System (GODAS) data provided by the NOAA PSL, Boulder, Colorado, USA, from their website at https://psl.noaa.gov

Temperature-at-depth data are geographically subset and spatially averaged using the pyFerret script `TatDepth_access.jnl` which can be found in the [Temperature_at_Depth](https://github.com/pwoodworth-jefcoats/climate-indicators/tree/main/Temperature_at_Depth) folder.  You could do this step in R, but I use [PyFerret](https://ferret.pmel.noaa.gov/Ferret/) because it's freely available software developed by NOAA specifically for working with large gridded datasets.  
\
